kikitalk Privacy Policy

Version and effective date: 2026-11-13-r18 · Updated: 2026-11-13

Operator: Li Hao (李浩) (individual developer) · Contact: 2114581274@qq.com

This is an archived version. Read the current version.

1. Scope and contact

kikitalk is provided and operated by Li Hao (李浩), an individual developer. For personal information protection, account or service questions, contact 2114581274@qq.com. The website and account service use https://kiki.group/; the separate voice chat service uses https://furby.top/. This policy applies to the current iOS app and website and does not imply that other planned clients are already available.

This service is available only to adults aged 18 or over. On first use, you must actively confirm that you meet the age requirement and read and agree to this policy and the Terms of Service. We do not initialize audio/video or instant messaging services before you agree. You can still read the legal documents and website introduction.

2. Accounts, profiles and usage records

The current version supports only Sign in with Apple. When you initiate sign-in and authorize it through the system, Apple supplies a user identifier scoped to this developer team, an identity token and a one-time authorization code. We submit the necessary authorization credentials to Apple over HTTPS to verify their authenticity, associate the verified identifier with an internal account, and store an encrypted refresh token to check authorization status and revoke authorization when you delete your account. Our server does not receive your Apple password. This version does not actively request or store your Apple name or email and does not use optional name or email fields in tokens to match accounts. The system Keychain stores this app’s session and Apple user identifier; we do not collect hardware serial numbers. The former ID sign-in method has been discontinued, and old test accounts are not automatically migrated to Apple accounts.

On first use, you must read the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy and actively tap “Agree and Continue”, also declaring that you are at least 18. The app obtains the current complete legal text and versions from our account service. Text included in the app or previously saved is for offline reading only; you can confirm the current version only after a successful online check. Your confirmation of the current version is saved locally. Normal restarts, signing in again after signing out, or cancelling Apple sign-in do not require another confirmation. An update to the documents or withdrawal of your consent requires confirmation again. Apple sign-in itself does not verify your actual age. The server uses a short-lived, one-time sign-in challenge and token validation to prevent replay of sign-in credentials. Failed or cancelled system authorization does not create a service account. The Apple user identifier is not displayed as your public nickname.

You must enter a nickname on first entry. You may add a bio, select a preset avatar or upload a photo that you choose from your photo library. The account service stores these details and, when you enter voice chat, synchronizes the necessary public user identifier, nickname, bio and avatar URL to the separate voice chat service to display members and enforce room permissions. It does not send Apple identity tokens, authorization codes or refresh tokens to that service. Other users may see your nickname, avatar, room name and content that you actively publish in a room. Do not enter or display national identity numbers, home addresses or other information that should not be public.

To provide room lists, favorites and history, the voice chat service stores room names, categories, background styles, status, associated public account identifiers and creation times, along with identifiers and times for favorited and visited rooms. History retains the 20 most recent rooms. Current voice rooms and usage records use the self-hosted service’s dataset; older voice sessions do not automatically resume in the new version. The account service stores notification preferences to control system alerts for the current account and whether message content is hidden. Turning off alerts or hiding content does not delete in-app messages.

The current version provides public in-app profiles, following, followers and mutual follows. Signed-in users who have completed a nickname and agreed to the current documents can view the necessary public nickname, bio, avatar, relationship counts and any joinable room you are hosting. We do not provide location, visitor tracking, or age or gender filters. The account service stores follows, in-app notifications and read status. The voice chat service is authoritative for room status and personal blocks. The two services synchronize necessary status through dedicated signed interfaces, without exchanging Apple identity credentials. Public profiles do not include Apple account information or private message text.

To distinguish actual use from merely holding a sign-in session, the account service records an internal account identifier, calendar day and necessary activity times when the app is used in the foreground. The voice chat service observes participation, speaking on a mic and short-term presence based on actual room connections, to generate deduplicated active-user, return-visit and cumulative-duration summaries. Account and voice activity records are retained for no more than 35 days; voice participation observations for no more than 30 days. Statistics begin when this feature is enabled, without reconstructing unknown history. Server lease renewals and automatic background refreshes do not count as account foreground activity. Associated identifiable activity records are cleared on withdrawal or account deletion. No third-party commercial analytics SDK is integrated.

We record applicable document versions, the document checksum, consent time, your confirmation of the age requirement and any withdrawal, to identify the text you confirmed, enforce your authorization choices and handle related disputes. These records do not contain your actual date of birth. To let network retries confirm withdrawal, a SHA-256 digest of the old session token used for a withdrawal request may be retained for up to 24 hours for idempotent confirmation. Expired records are removed on later withdrawal requests or service startup. Withdrawal records do not additionally store IP addresses or hardware device information.

Mic-seat relationship displays are a feature of this version. After you accept this policy and the Terms of Service, birth information you have entered is used for server-side BaZi relationship calculations. Your entered MBTI type and zodiac sign derived from your original Gregorian birthday are public labels visible to users permitted to view your profile or room. The profile page no longer has separate participation or sharing switches. Unknown information may be left blank, and no default birth time is invented to generate BaZi. Your birth date, calendar and leap-month selection, local clock time, birth region and representative coordinates, time zone, true solar time and Four Pillars are available only to you through private profile interfaces; they are not sent to other users’ clients or to the voice media service. Birthplace is chosen from a region directory. We do not request device location permission, automatically use your current location or send birth information to AI services.

3. Room communication and device information

The current version uses the open-source LiveKit client to connect to our self-hosted signaling, media and room service nodes, providing voice rooms, eight mic seats and an audience, approval queues, text interaction and announcements. Your live voice is processed when you turn on your microphone. Room text, the sender’s public identifier and necessary time and room information are processed and transmitted to the relevant room members. Rooms offer five preset backgrounds that adapt to the device’s light or dark appearance; hosts can choose one when creating or editing a room. Video broadcasting and sound effects are not currently available. Turning off your microphone or leaving the room stops the corresponding live collection. Minimizing a room to an in-app floating bubble does not mean you have left: an active audio session may continue in the background. Explicitly turn off the microphone or leave when you want to stop communicating.

Within the signed-in community, you can follow other users, view public profiles and start text private messages without a mutual follow. Each sender can send up to five messages before the other person first replies; once they reply, both can continue. Public nicknames, bios, avatars, relationships and necessary times are shown to authorized users. Private message text is available only to the participants in that conversation; operators cannot freely browse all private messages. Following or unfollowing does not change private messaging permission. Clearing your own chat history affects only the records visible to you, not the other person’s view, and does not reset the first-contact limit. To enforce that limit, the server stores minimal state consisting of the number of messages sent by each party and whether a reply has occurred. This state remains during normal use and is deleted on withdrawal of privacy consent or account deletion. Expiry of message text does not reopen the sending allowance. Existing history remains viewable within its retention period. A block by either party hides the relevant social profiles, notifications and private messages. Reception in public voice rooms remains subject to the rules below.

Private messages have a rolling retention period of up to 30 days. Social notifications and the status of reports you submitted are retained for up to 30 days and support read-status queries. After you actively allow notifications, Apple Push Notification service (APNs) can deliver alerts for private messages and in-app interactions. System notifications do not replace actual in-app read status or content permissions. Reported text retained as needed for investigation is kept for up to 30 days. Historical records and media from retired features are retained only as restricted rollback material and are no longer provided through live features. Section 6 explains restricted backup cleanup. Retiring a feature or deleting it from the interface does not mean that database WAL files and historical backups are all physically destroyed at the same time.

To send system alerts to authorized devices, the app obtains the device push token that Apple provides for this app and generates a random installation identifier. The account service stores the token, installation identifier, development or production environment, authorization status and necessary update times, associated with the current service account and a valid sign-in session. The random installation identifier is not a hardware serial number or advertising identifier. Push tokens are used only to deliver this app’s messages, are encrypted in online storage, and are not displayed as public information or as a device list available for operators to browse.

The account server sends system pushes through Apple APNs, not through the separate voice media server. By default, alerts may show the sender’s current nickname, private message text or an in-app interaction summary. You can enable “Hide Message Content” in the app under Settings → Notifications. Alerts sent afterward use fixed generic wording without message text or the sender’s nickname. Pushes do not include photos, image content or room names. Actual display remains subject to iOS notification preview settings. The payload also includes a random event identifier for verification and navigation after sign-in, and a necessary badge count. Apple processes the device push token, app identifier, the above payload and information required by its service to deliver notifications. After a notification is tapped, the account service must still verify the current account, consent and content permissions. A notification itself grants no access.

A system push device binding is retained until its session expires or it has not been updated for 30 consecutive days, whichever comes first. Pending alerts are retained for up to 24 hours. Final delivery records and random events used to verify taps are retained for up to seven days. To prevent a late old request from re-binding a device after sign-out or an account change, the server retains a necessary binding revision watermark under a non-public index derived from the random installation identifier for up to 30 days. The watermark stores neither the original installation identifier nor the push token. Signing out clears the corresponding session binding. Withdrawal and account deletion clear that account’s bindings and pending records. Notifications already accepted by Apple and restricted backups are cleared according to their actual processing rules.

To connect, adapt to devices and investigate quality issues, the SDK and self-hosted services may process room and public user identifiers, device model, operating system and version, network type and connection status, IP address and necessary communication statistics. The client reports only available connection quality, audio route and diagnostic values such as RTT, jitter and packet loss; missing values are marked unknown. Server quality samples are held in memory for no more than five minutes and at most the latest 1,000 samples, and are cleared on restart. Operations staff use separate management dashboards with divided permissions to view aggregate service and host metrics; these dashboards do not expose Apple credentials or live audio content. Community moderation requires separate authorization. Authorized staff can access only necessary report information and text evidence saved as needed to handle reports, and perform recorded voice-chat moderation. Components are listed at https://kiki.group/privacy/sdk/.

To investigate failures in creating or entering rooms and errors or warnings during use, the client and the two service servers record necessary incident events: public account identifier and nickname, room identifier (excluding the room name), action and failure stage, preset error code and severity, occurrence and receipt times, duration, HTTP status, random incident, action and request identifiers, iOS or iPadOS type, and app and system versions. These events do not upload raw error text, request URLs, session tokens, Apple identity identifiers, IP addresses, device names or room audio and text content. Authorized voice operations staff can query events by public nickname or identifier. The client stores pending events in a private file excluded from system backups, limited to 100 events and seven days. It retries when connectivity returns and clears them on sign-out, account change, withdrawal or account deletion. The account service may provide a restricted persistent retry queue for events such as voice authorization failures, retained for up to seven days; event content is deleted after successful delivery. Voice-service incident events are retained for up to seven days with a global maximum of 10,000, evicting older records early at the limit. Repeated quality warnings may be merged or rate-limited, so this is not a complete activity log. Withdrawal or account deletion clears associated online and pending events, with necessary short-lived authorization state preventing old events from arriving after withdrawal and being stored again.

The current app has no recording, playback, AI transcription, voiceprint or facial identification features, and no advertising tracking or commercial analytics SDK. Necessary relay of live audio and brief diagnostics do not mean that recordings are stored long term. The room text service assigns sequence numbers and provides a rolling history of at most the latest 200 messages for up to two hours. Closing a room, or an author withdrawing consent or deleting their account, clears the corresponding online service text. This rolling window is not a physical erasure deadline for database WAL files or restricted historical backups.

You can report a room, user or room message, select a reason and add necessary details. The voice chat service checks participation records and saves, as needed, the report identifier, reporter and reported party’s public account identifiers and nicknames, room information, submission time, reason, details and a text snapshot of a reported message for investigation and feedback. Reports and text evidence are retained for up to 30 days. Reporting does not automatically record or replay audio; basic text-term filtering is not comprehensive voice moderation. Warnings and moderation notices are retained for up to 30 days; necessary action audits and receipts preventing duplicate actions for up to 90 days.

The voice chat service stores your block list to filter the blocked users’ room text and audio for you while you use the service. You can unblock them in community safety settings. Blocking does not automatically remove the other person from a public room and cannot guarantee that they cannot hear voice you actively publish there. Withdrawal or account deletion clears associated reports, blocks, notifications and unnecessary audit details and target identifiers. Necessary voice restrictions may remain until expiry after withdrawal to prevent restrictions being evaded through withdrawal. Account deletion clears that account’s restriction state.

Social reports may concern public profiles or private messages in which you participate. After verifying content and participation eligibility, the server retains the report identifier, reporter and reported party’s public accounts and nicknames, reason, details and text evidence as needed for up to 30 days. Staff separately authorized for community moderation may read only evidence associated with a case and issue warnings, remove violating content, impose temporary social posting restrictions, lift restrictions or dismiss reports. Social restrictions limit private message sending and new follows. They do not replace voice bans or prevent Apple sign-in, withdrawal or account deletion. Related audits and receipts preventing duplicate actions are retained for up to 90 days. Withdrawal or account deletion clears associated social content, conversations, relationships, notifications and reports and removes unnecessary identifiable details from audits. Active restrictions may remain until expiry after withdrawal and are cleared on account deletion.

When you agree to the current documents and use the service, usable BaZi information you have entered automatically participates in relationship calculations among members currently on mic in the room. Sharing of MBTI and birthday-derived zodiac signs follows this policy without repeated confirmation on the profile page. Room members see only relationship categories and permitted summaries, not other people’s birth information, Four Pillars or pillar-by-pillar reasoning. Results use fixed versions of cultural or community rules and are for conversation only. They do not represent actual relationship quality or future outcomes and may express only a few relationship characteristics. You can correct or clear your details under Me. After an update, clearing, withdrawal or account deletion, the server invalidates the corresponding old results and connected clients update on refresh. We cannot guarantee immediate withdrawal of content independently recorded by other users.

4. Permissions and choices

The microphone is used only for speaking in voice chat. System permission is requested when you actively turn on your microphone. Denying or disabling it does not affect listening, text profiles, legal documents or other features that do not need sound capture. Video broadcasting is hidden in this version, and camera permission is not actively requested.

When setting an avatar, you use the system photo picker to choose the image you want to provide. We do not read your entire library. Only an avatar you select and confirm saving is uploaded. The client and server convert it to static JPEG, resize it and remove photo metadata. You can also use a preset avatar. We do not currently request location, contacts or advertising tracking permissions. You can manage granted microphone, camera and photo-related permissions in iOS Settings; exact paths vary by system version. Full details: https://kiki.group/privacy/permissions/.

Before you confirm consent, the app accesses only the public legal-document interface of our account service over HTTPS to obtain and verify the latest complete documents. It sends no account credentials, cookies, device identifiers or push tokens, creates no account, initializes no audio/video service and requests no notification permission. Necessary network communication supplies the server with an IP address; the system may offer a network access choice. Saved text remains readable offline; you can confirm after obtaining the current documents online. On first use, after you agree to the current documents and before Apple sign-in, the app checks connectivity through our service’s health check without account credentials, cookies or push tokens, then requests system notification permission. The device system decides whether and how to show a network access prompt. If connection fails, you can check your network and retry; failure is not automatically treated as refusal of permission. Once you have decided notification permission, the system request is not repeated. Denial or an unfinished authorization request does not block sign-in, in-app private messages, interactions or voice chat. You can enable alerts later from message or notification settings, adjust banners, sounds and badges in system settings, or stop alerts for the current account with the in-app switch. Actual push registration and token binding occur only after valid sign-in and permission for the relevant alerts. Signing out, changing accounts, withdrawing consent or deleting an account stops the corresponding device binding and clears local notification state. Notifications already accepted by Apple may not be immediately retractable and may arrive late; tapping still requires account and permission checks.

5. Third-party processing and public visibility

Live voice chat uses the open-source LiveKit SDK and its WebRTC and native bridge dependencies. Room authorization, signaling, media relay and service messages are processed by our configured self-hosted nodes; LiveKit Cloud room services are not configured. The account server and voice chat server are separate. After account authorization, a dedicated signed server interface exchanges it for voice credentials. The app holds neither the inter-service secret nor LiveKit administrative keys. The current production iOS target no longer uses Tencent TRTC, Room Engine, TUILiveKit or IM to process the new voice chat. Reference projects in the repository are outside the current app’s enabled scope.

Sign in with Apple uses the iOS AuthenticationServices framework and Apple identity services. We submit the authorization codes, tokens and app identifiers necessary for verification, token exchange, status checks and revocation to Apple. Apple processes account and device information according to its Sign in with Apple & Privacy information and privacy policy. This app does not read your Apple password, account files or contacts. Service information: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/zh-cn/sign-in-with-apple/.

Nicknames, avatars, voice and text you actively make public in a room are received by the relevant users. We explain the display scope and ask for confirmation when you publish profile information or enable the relevant communication feature. Other users may independently record or forward what they see or hear, so share carefully. We do not sell your personal information. For lawful disclosure to competent authorities, a lawful change of business operator or other situations requiring separate authorization, we fulfill the applicable legal duties of notice, authorization and protection.

System notifications use Apple’s UserNotifications framework and APNs, provided by Apple. Necessary device tokens, app identifiers, alert payloads and event identifiers are submitted to Apple to deliver alerts to devices authorized by users. Alerts may by default contain the sender’s nickname, private message text or an in-app interaction summary. After “Hide Message Content” is enabled, subsequent alerts use generic wording. No photos or image content are submitted in pushes. Apple processes information for its device and notification services according to its privacy policy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/zh-cn/.

6. Storage locations, retention and security

Service accounts, profiles and avatars are stored on our account server in mainland China. Rooms, authorization mappings and usage records are stored on our separate voice chat server in mainland China and in necessary restricted operations backups. Local Keychain items and image caches remain on your device. Apple sign-in and system notifications separately access Apple identity and APNs services. Apple handles necessary authorization credentials or device tokens and alert payloads under its service rules; the app does not control its networks or processing locations. Self-hosted business nodes in mainland China do not mean that all Apple authentication and push processing occurs there. Where personal information is provided across borders, the operator fulfills the applicable procedures and notice duties.

Account profiles, favorites and history are retained while needed for the corresponding services. You can edit profiles, remove favorites or request account deletion. Account sessions normally last 30 days and can renew during valid use. Voice service credentials use renewable authorization lasting up to 15 minutes; room-entry credentials normally last five minutes. These are credential validity periods, not deadlines at which all service records are automatically deleted. After sign-out or withdrawal, the device first stops media and the server revokes voice authorization. A cleanup intent is retained for retries during network failures, and clients cannot extend expired voice leases themselves. Image caches may be removed by the system or updated by the app.

Consent, withdrawal and necessary security records are retained only as needed to identify authorization status, handle disputes or fulfill legal duties. The newly introduced routine consistent backups are restricted on their respective servers, normally rotate over seven days, and validate isolated copies of databases and associated files. If validation of a new backup fails, the previous successful copy is retained and operations staff are alerted. An older copy may therefore remain beyond seven days during a fault; overdue managed copies are cleared after successful recovery. These backups do not directly serve online users and do not replace off-site disaster recovery. Earlier manual operations backups have no uniform automatic deletion deadline. Section 3 describes rolling retention for online text and diagnostics. You can use the public email to request verification or deletion of applicable records and backup copies. We handle requests according to the specific records and legal retention requirements and explain any inability to delete immediately. We do not present an unverified fixed number of days as an implemented deletion commitment.

Service requests use HTTPS. Sign-in sessions are protected by the system Keychain, digest checks and server access controls. Apple refresh tokens in the service database and pending revocation queue are encrypted using a separate server-side key; private keys do not enter the app. Routine server access logs are disabled. Failures may still generate necessary error records, and communication components may generate diagnostics needed for normal operation. Security measures cannot eliminate all network risks. If a personal information security incident occurs, we take remedial action and fulfill notification and other duties as required by law.

Private birth information is stored on the account server while the relationship feature is provided. You can correct or clear it through BaZi under Me; MBTI has a separate editor. When you view or edit private information, the device processes it only in the current page’s memory. It is not written to public profile caches, system pushes or ordinary analytics events. Other users’ clients receive only relationship results. Clearing birth information, withdrawing privacy consent or deleting your account clears the corresponding online private information. Restricted backups remain subject to this section’s retention rules. The server automatically handles regional time zones and historical clock rules using fixed rules. A duplicated local clock time during a historical backward change defaults to its first occurrence; a nonexistent time prompts you to check it.

7. Access, correction, withdrawal and account deletion

Under Me you can view and edit your nickname and avatar and view favorites and history. Settings let you sign out, withdraw privacy consent or request account deletion. Withdrawal stops services requiring that consent and ends the current communication session. It does not affect prior lawful processing and is not account deletion or automatic deletion of all existing data. Using the service again requires confirmation of the applicable documents. Withdrawal also clears push bindings and pending records, online social relationships, private conversations, notifications and associated reports; the other participant will also no longer be able to read that conversation through the online service. Content already obtained on devices and restricted backups follow their actual cleanup and retention rules.

Account deletion removes your account, sign-in identity, sessions and uploaded avatar from the online account service database and sends a durable cleanup request to the separate voice service to revoke voice authorization and clear that identity’s profile snapshots, favorites, history and messages. The voice service handles active rooms according to host transfer or room-ending rules. Cleanup intent continues to retry during network failures. Ended room identifiers and anonymized display records may remain to preserve the integrity of other members’ records. Deletion also requests revocation of Apple authorization. If Apple is temporarily unavailable, the service account is still deleted; encrypted tokens needed to finish revocation are retried in a restricted queue and deleted after success. Historical backups and data in older third-party services are not all destroyed at the same moment. Contact 2114581274@qq.com for further cleanup. Signing in with Apple again creates a new service account and cannot restore deleted information.

To copy, export or delete other personal information, or lawfully request restricted processing, transfer or similar rights, email the public contact address. To prevent impersonation, we may need to verify identity using existing account information. Do not directly send full identity-document photos or account secrets. We respond within a reasonable period after verification. If a request cannot lawfully be fulfilled, we explain why and provide available remedies or further feedback channels.

Under Me, separate BaZi and MBTI entries let you view, edit or clear your details. The zodiac sign is generated from the birthday you enter; profile editing is not offered inside rooms. Entering birth information is not actual age verification. An unknown birth time may remain blank. Missing information results only in an indication that the relevant relationship cannot yet be calculated; no result is fabricated. If you disagree with the current handling of relationship information, you may decline or withdraw consent in Settings. Returning to the service requires active confirmation of the current version.

8. Adults only and policy updates

This service is not available to anyone under 18. A general consent action does not replace measures to protect minors. If you are under 18, do not register, sign in or submit personal information. If a minor is found to have used the service by mistake, the minor or a guardian can contact the public email; we will verify and handle the account and information.

For material changes to this policy, particularly purposes, methods, data categories or your main rights, we update the version and notify you through in-app prompts or similar means. Where renewed consent is legally required, we obtain it first. You can read the current version in the app or on the website at any time. Historical text is available through the version links on the pages.
